title: 3D printing austenitic stainless steel 316L by cold spray process: optimum post‑spraying heat treatment conditions
InformationInFigures: Yes. microhardness (Fig. 11, 14, and 16), grain sizes (Fig. 10, 13, 15), select tensile values (Fig. 18)

preSprayedProperties.Powder_Morphology: predominantly irregular-shaped particles with a minor fraction exhibiting spherical morphology. particles exhibit surface porosity. dominant presence of austenite phase, and dendrite and ferrite phases present.
preSprayedProperties.Powder_Particle_Size_Other: 21.4% of particles are below 20 μm, 15.8% of particles are between 20 and 25 μm, 49% of particles are between 25 and 36 μm, 11.6% of particles are between 36 and 45 μm, and 2.2% of particles are above 45 μm

experimentalProperties.Additional_Manufacturing_Processes_Descr: Each block was subsequently sectioned using a wet cutting machine with diamond disc into four smaller samples measuring 20 x 20 x 10 mm, which were used for various experimental analyses. blocks were then  subjected to a polishing process using Struer Polishing machine. The samples were polished using Struer polishing method for stainless steel, including using SiC 320, Largo, Mol, Nab and Chem grinding surface, achieving a surface fnish of 0.1 µm. The polished sample was etched using Kalling’s reagent to reveal its microstructural features.

resultsValues.Microstructural_Features: microstructure retained the prior dendrite austenite as in the as-received powder. The plastic deformation by cold spray can be seen in the shape of dendrite austenite grain. The gap between particles grain boundaries (GBs) gap is on an average, 0.5 µm. the dendrite grain boundary of each particle has composition of Ni, Mo, and Mn higher than inside the grain, especially much higher for Mn which indicates there is a segregation of these elements at the dendrite GBs.
